evals.prompt: Pathways Workforce Partners ($3.5M, Ohio) has never had a negotiated indirect rate. We just received a subaward from our state workforce board under a federal Department of Labor award the state received in March 2025. Our budget: $180,000 salaries and fringe, $25,000 supplies and travel, a $90,000 subaward to Clark Community College, $15,000 equipment, and $12,000 in participant support stipends. The state says it caps indirect at 10%. What indirect can we charge?
evals.expected_output: Confirms award applicability and de minimis eligibility, computes MTDC with the correct exclusions and subaward limit, challenges the 10% cap's authority, and stops for qualified review.
assertions: Checks which version of the Uniform Guidance applies to the award (the October 1, 2024 revisions) before selecting a percentage
Explains the de minimis rate is up to 15% of MTDC, is optional, and is available only without a current federal negotiated rate
Builds MTDC including only the first $50,000 of the subaward and excluding equipment and participant support

Asks for the written authority behind the state's 10% cap, noting a pass-through generally cannot force a lower rate than an eligible recipient's de minimis election unless statute or regulation requires it
Quantifies any unrecovered amount as an organizational subsidy rather than assuming it counts as cost share
Recommends review by a CPA or indirect-cost specialist before submission

evals.prompt: board member keeps asking what our afterschool program 'really costs' per kid. 140 kids, $410k direct. rent, finance, HR are shared across our 4 programs. how do i figure it out
evals.expected_output: Walks through a true-cost-per-unit analysis that adds a documented share of shared cost pools, divides by units of service, and compares to what funders pay to reveal the subsidy.
assertions: Adds the program's share of each shared cost pool using a documented, benefit-based basis (e.g., square footage for rent, headcount for HR)
Divides total cost by units of service (e.g., participants) to get a per-unit cost
Compares the true per-unit cost to what funders or fees actually pay to show the annual unrestricted subsidy
Distinguishes this internal true-cost figure from a federal compliance or de minimis indirect rate
Suggests presenting the subsidy math alongside the program's mission case for the board

evals.prompt: We have a 2023 NICRA with HHS that uses a $25,000-per-subaward base. Our program officer at a different agency says under the new rules we can just bump the subaward base to $50,000, and also use the 15% de minimis on this one grant since it's higher than our negotiated rate. OK to do both?
evals.expected_output: Says no to both: honor the NICRA's approved base until revised, de minimis is unavailable with a current negotiated rate, and switching methods per grant fails consistency; escalate for qualified review.
assertions: Says not to replace the NICRA's $25,000 subaward base with $50,000 unless the agreement is appropriately revised
States de minimis is not available while the organization has a current federal negotiated rate
Warns against switching methods on individual grants to maximize recovery (consistency requirement)
Recommends checking the award's rule version/effective date and escalating to a grants/finance specialist or the cognizant agency before acting

Will we run short of cash in March while we wait on grant reimbursements?
